classification.summary: getBuyBackPrice divides the contract's ETH reserve by token.totalSupply() even though the contract itself held ~79% of that supply as unsold inventory, so purchase() sold that inventory for a fraction of the reserve share it entitles the buyer to and buyBack() immediately redeemed it at the full per-supply price, letting a flash-loaned purchase/buyBack loop drain the reserve.

sources.note: onchain review: OMPxContract 0x09a80172ed7335660327cd664876b5df6fe06108 was created 2018-04-10T18:22:23Z at block 5417094 by 0xeb79db7b4ce44bfb549104cafc8f51cc93a686fb, unrelated to attack sender 0x40d115198d71cab59668b51dd112a07d273d5831 or its attack contract 0xfaddf57d079b01e53d1fe3476cc83e9bcc705854. It is a verified non-proxy Solidity 0.4 contract and its codehash is identical (0x3d5e00bc4c97981d2b270895a01c69466c564f9a42f4140b9d7eeae4bae1b9bf) at the creation block and at the block before the incident, so the age is measured from deployment: 6.33 years. Mechanism confirmed against state at block 20468779: OMPX totalSupply 2,269,323e18 with 1,799,614e18 (79.3%) held by the victim itself, ETH reserve 5.6955 ETH, and the discount coefficients read from discounts(i) are 198/190/180/150 against descPrecision 100, i.e. purchase is nominally at a 1.5-2x markup - the profit comes from the totalSupply denominator, not from a discount. The trace shows 7 purchase/buyBack rounds: round one pays 100 ETH with 93.2257 ETH refunded (net 6.7743 ETH) and is bought back for 9.2914 ETH. Loss not recorded in USD: the victim's ETH balance fell from 5.695503 to 1.322633 ETH, i.e. 4.372870 ETH, matching the 4.37 ETH in the DeFiHackLabs PoC; the ~$107k headline circulated elsewhere is irreconcilable with that (the PoC itself quotes ~$11.5k). Order-of-magnitude sanity check only (ETH ~ $2,400 in Aug 2024, so ~$10k): above the $1,000 floor.
loss converted at the incident timestamp (1722938291) via DefiLlama coins: 4.37 ETH x $2,465.70 = $10,775
